title: Conditionals
subtitle: Zero to mixed conditionals, inversion, and other if-structures

theory.title: Zero conditional (if / when / whenever + present, present)

rows.use: General or scientific facts and definitions
rows.example: If you **heat** ice, it **melts**.

theory.title: First conditional (if + present, will + bare infinitive / imperative)

rows.use: Real conditions in the present or future and their results
rows.example: If we **keep** dumping plastic in rivers, wildlife **will suffer**.
If the press office **rings**, **take** a message and I'll call them later.

blocks.text: Other modals and semi-modals can replace **will** in the result clause: **be going to, can, could, may, might, shall, should, have to, ought to**.
blocks.note: We **might** avoid the worst of the crisis if we **change** how we live now.

theory.title: Second conditional (if + past simple / past continuous, would + bare infinitive)

rows.use: Hypothetical conditions now or in the future, and their hypothetical results
rows.example: What **would** the council **do** if there **was** a cyclone in the region?

blocks.text: **Might** and **could** can replace **would** in the result clause.
blocks.note: If the forecast **were** better, we **could** eat outside.

items: In British English, both **was** and **were** are possible after **if** with first and third person singular. **Were** is more common in a formal style. In American English, **were** is usual.
UK: If I **was/were** a trader, I'd put money on Lena arriving late.
US: If I **were** a trader, I'd put money on Lena arriving late.
In both varieties, **were** is usual in **If I were you, …**

theory.title: Third conditional (if + past perfect, would have + past participle)

rows.use: Hypothetical conditions in the past and their past results
rows.example: Far more people **would have been stranded** by the storm if the barrier **hadn't been** raised.

blocks.text: **Might, could** and **should** can replace **would** in the result clause.
blocks.note: If you **hadn't had** such a lucky break, you **could have lost** everything.

rows.example: You **might not be** in this mess if you **hadn't started** betting.
If I **were** you, I **would have told** Nina to buy her own ticket.
**Should** the drought **continue**, many families **will be forced** to leave. (= If the drought should continue … / If the drought continues …)
**Were we to** abandon fossil fuels tomorrow, it **would still take** decades for the climate to recover. (= If we were to stop … / If we stopped …)
**Had** Darwin **not visited** those islands, he **might never have developed** his theory. (= If Darwin hadn't visited …)

blocks.text: When the inverted verb is negative, **not** comes after the subject.
blocks.note: **Had we not** attended the briefing, we would have missed the council's plans.

blocks.text: When the **if** clause comes before the result, we usually separate the two clauses with a comma. When the result comes first, we do not use a comma.
blocks.note: If you share a lift, you can cut your costs. · You can cut your costs if you share a lift.

rows.example: We'll hike this weekend **as long as** the weather holds.
You can keep a dog **provided that** you look after it properly.
Applications are accepted **on condition that** candidates are over 18.
**Supposing** the price of oil tripled overnight. What do you think would happen?

rows.use: if it wasn't / weren't for + noun
rows.example: I'd feel quite lonely **if it weren't for** my dog, Buster.
**Were it not for** Buster, I think I'd be quite lonely.
**But for** your support, I wouldn't have been able to quit.

rows.use: if it hadn't been for + noun
rows.example: **If it hadn't been for** your support, I wouldn't have been able to quit.

rows.use: had it not been for + noun
rows.example: **Had it not been for** your support, I wouldn't have been able to quit.
**If you (should) happen to** see Davina, ask whether she would look after the cats.
**If you should** see Davina, ask whether she would look after the cats.
**If you happened to** see someone drop litter in the street, what would you do?
Do you think it would cut pollution **if the government were to** introduce a new tax on petrol?
Are you worried about the climate? **If so**, you might want to join a campaign group.
You should have the boiler serviced, **otherwise** you'll waste a lot of energy.
**Unless** governments act now, the environment is really going to suffer.
**In case of** fire, leave the building by the nearest emergency exit.
Take a coat with you **in case** the weather gets worse.

rows.use: To mean 'if it is true that'
rows.example: **If** you were at the meeting, why didn't you raise the recycling issue?

rows.use: To mean 'if you are willing to'
rows.example: **If** you'll follow me, I'll show you into the manager's office.

rows.use: To mean 'I'm saying this in case'
rows.example: **If** you like aquariums, the one in Singapore is spectacular.

exercises.title: B · Rewrite with the words given
exercises.instruction: Rewrite using an appropriate conditional form, starting with the words given. Write the rest of the sentence.

items.prompt:
Sue didn't get me a birthday present, which is why I didn't get her one.
If Sue
acceptedAnswers: had got me a birthday present, I would have got her one.
had given me a birthday present, I would have given her one.
had got me a birthday present, I'd have got her one.

items.prompt:
We didn't pay them on time because they made a mistake with our order.
If they
acceptedAnswers: hadn't made a mistake with our order, we would have paid them on time.
hadn't made a mistake with our order, we'd have paid them on time.

items.prompt:
The climate is undergoing such radical changes that scientists are worried.
If
acceptedAnswers: the climate weren't undergoing such radical changes, scientists wouldn't be worried.
the climate wasn't undergoing such radical changes, scientists wouldn't be worried.
the climate were not undergoing such radical changes, scientists would not be worried.

items.prompt:
Did California become an important area because they found gold there?
Would
acceptedAnswers: California have become an important area if they hadn't found gold there?
California have become an important area if they had not found gold there?

items.prompt:
It's the sunset that attracts tourists to that place.
If it
acceptedAnswers: weren't for the sunset, tourists wouldn't be attracted to that place.
wasn't for the sunset, tourists wouldn't be attracted to that place.
weren't for the sunset, tourists would not be attracted to that place.

items.prompt:
There was a traffic jam on the motorway so I was late for my interview.
If there
acceptedAnswers: hadn't been a traffic jam on the motorway, I wouldn't have been late for my interview.
hadn't been a traffic jam on the motorway, I would not have been late for my interview.

items.prompt:
I suggest you use a sunblock, and then you won't go red.
If I were
acceptedAnswers: you, I'd use a sunblock and then you won't go red.
you, I would use a sunblock and then you won't go red.
you, I'd use a sunblock so you won't go red.

items.prompt:
The accident happened as a result of the driver not paying attention to the road.
If the driver
acceptedAnswers: had been paying attention to the road, the accident wouldn't have happened.
had paid attention to the road, the accident wouldn't have happened.
had been paying attention to the road, the accident would not have happened.

exercises.title: C · Verb forms
exercises.instruction: Complete using the correct form of the verbs in brackets. Add any other words you need.

items.prompt: So, today marks one year since I became a Park Ranger. If I ___ that then, I never would have had so many fantastic experiences. (do)
If I hadn't done that then, I never ___ so many fantastic experiences. (have)
If you ___ me now, I would say that I knew nothing when I started, but I've learnt a huge amount. (ask)
On a typical day, I'll deal with complaints, check on the running of the park and lead guided tours, if any ___. (book)
If it's low season, I ___ time to check on forest management and fire control measures. (have)
It can get stressful at times, especially if visitors to the park ___ lost or injured. (get)
We had a case last week, which wouldn't ___ if the woman involved had been a bit more careful. (happen)
We had a case last week, which wouldn't have happened if the woman involved ___ a bit more careful. (be)
You see, if you ___ around a large National Park like this without a map, you're bound to get lost. (wander)
This particular case might ___ so bad if it hadn't started raining. (be)
This particular case might not have been so bad if it ___ raining. (start)
She was only wearing light clothes, so she was wet through and freezing when we found her. I dread to think what might ___ if we hadn't! (happen)

items.prompt:

acceptedAnswers: won the contract if it hadn't been for Debbie's fantastic presentation.

items.prompt:
